summary: Right-handed basketball jump shot at release: airborne near the top of the jump, shooting arm extended high toward the rim, wrist snapped down in a gooseneck follow-through, guide hand up at the side.

environment.text: Rim 3.05 m high, {fwd:rim:pelvis} cm ahead; the ball has just left the fingertips on a high arc (release angle about 50-55 deg).

cameras.name: front_low
cameras.text: Defender's-eye view from in front, arm and gooseneck wrist sharp.

cameras.name: side
cameras.text: Profile: extended arm, flexed wrist, ball arcing up.

cameras.name: baseline_wide
cameras.text: Wide from the baseline, rim in frame, crowd blurred.

rules.why: arm nearly extended at release (about 45 deg at release, extending into the follow-through)
shoulder flexion about 103-114 deg at release
wrist snapped forward (gooseneck), fingers toward the rim
legs extended, knee about 13-16 deg at release
high release: hand height about 1.28-1.40 x body height
released near the top of the jump

text.action: a basketball player releasing a right-handed jump shot at the top of the jump
text.core: Airborne with legs straight and toes pointed down; body upright; right shooting arm extended high and forward toward the rim, elbow almost straight; wrist snapped down in a gooseneck, fingers pointing at the rim; ball just off the fingertips; left guide hand still up beside the head, palm facing sideways, not pushing.
cues: high release at or just before the top of the jump
gooseneck follow-through, fingers toward the hoop
guide hand stays up and quiet
kinetic: ball spinning backward off the fingertips, seams blurred
jersey lifted slightly by the jump
shadow of the shooter small on the court below

sources.cite: Irawan & Prastiwi 2022, JPES: knee 167 deg and elbow 135 deg inside angles at release (convention assumed)
Vencurik et al. 2021, IJERPH 18:934: shoulder 103-114 deg at release, elite U16/U18
Coach's Clipboard / FIBA WABC 2.7.5: wrist flick, gooseneck follow-through
Cabarkapa et al. 2022: release hand height / body height 1.40 (proficient) vs 1.28
Okazaki & Rodacki 2012, JSSM 11:231: release height 2.33-2.46 m, release near the jump peak
